issue_context.title: MaxWorkingSet supported platforms
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3130ac980c97c0664eddb04411f8f765a9f908d8/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/ref/System.Diagnostics.Process.cs#L45

The code specifies supported platforms as Windows only.

However, the [documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/docs/blob/3588fdadac34bee137fe519d50c9a187d704d1fd/docs/core/compatibility/unsupported-apis.md) mentions it throws in Linux only, which means both Windows and macOS are supported.

I think macOS should be missing in either the documentation or the supported platforms attribute.
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @eiriktsarpalis
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

Seems OSX is using BSD code and BSD seems to be supporting MaxWorkingSet:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/src/System.Diagnostics.Process.csproj#L288

probably the attribute should be added then, not sure if this qualifies as 5.0 bug.
@terrajobst any clues how much do we want to have SupportedOSPlatformAttribute up to date for 5.0?

From looking at [the code](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/src/System/Diagnostics/Process.BSD.cs#L62-L63) it seems `MaxWorkingSet` is only supported for the current process and throws PNSE for all other processes. That's why the tool still flagged the API as not being supported.

I'd say based [on our principles](https://github.com/dotnet/designs/blob/master/accepted/2020/windows-specific-apis/windows-specific-apis.md#partially-supported-apis) it seems we should be marking this API as supported on `macOS`.

> @terrajobst any clues how much do we want to have SupportedOSPlatformAttribute up to date for 5.0?

The ones we put should ideally be a 100% correct, but I don't think of bugs like this as ship stoppers. In fact, I'm quite certain we'll have to tweak some of them based on customer feedback.
I would be supportive of adding `[SupportedOSPlatform("macos")]` to this API. I recommend we go ahead and get that fix into master and request approval for an RC2 port this week.
Ok looking again this looks like for OSX/BSD it has only limited support (only works for the current process) so I'm leaning toward updating docs rather than adding attribute
Do we have a platform identifier for FreeBSD? We should also add an attribute for that if that's the case.

Testing of this fix surfaced https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/4168; these annotations are currently being ignored because of the assembly-level `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]` attribute.

We are going to revisit the analyzer logic for the scenario.

> what do you think?

In my opinion, it's also not release-blocking.

> wrap calls to set these properties on `macos` or `freebsd` with `#pragma warning disable CA1416`

@jeffhandley Thank you for providing the workaround. Anyone who is going to hit this issue with 5.0 and search for it on the internet should be unblocked thanks to that!

> @Youssef1313; I presume you found it by way of reading code and documentation--is that right?

Yes I just came across that doc page and wanted to check its accuracy. So I took some random APIs from the doc and compared them with the code here.
Thanks, all.  I've moved this to 6.0.0 and I will close the 5.0-rc2 port PR without merging it.
